notes.title: Lifecraft is evolving again!
notes.notes:
[h2][b]HELLO EVERYONE!
[/b][/h2]

Here we are to update you about upcoming updates for Lifecraft! We spent a lot of time implementing a flexible system to manage and let organism live inside and outside your organism. Things started little but during the way we understood it was necessary to have a proper goal-oriented AI system to manage what the cells will do and how they'll handle their priorities so the system itself became [b]HUGE[/b].

That's why at some point we changed our focus to start working on a very useful feature, both for us and both for you: a blueprint system together with library and a way to share the schematics beween players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f41add3fd449c87358377c27a7258eb745f885e4.png[/img]

[b]BLUEPRINT SYSTEM[/b]

The much requested blueprints system is coming! We plan to roll it out in the next 1-2 weeks on the nightly build.
The first version will be available only on sandbox to be tested, then we'll add it to survival games too (which requires more work as bluepirnt must be built by diffusers!).

You will be able to save map selections as blueprints, save them into a library and share them between players and your other worlds. Blueprints can be rotated and flipped to suit any need!

We also added a special label plate structure used just to show an icon which can be a nice aesthetics touch to your blueprint (or worlds).

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/8a7d5b387e535850a8ca2870554b51a22e5b445e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/0e067ce4408a8b4e1bd42896350ab88f42906092.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f2c63485bc6f9aff5d29adcf389581de27c863f1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f41add3fd449c87358377c27a7258eb745f885e4.png[/img]

[b]QUALITY OF LIFE UPDATES 
[/b]
We're also constantly working on QOL updates, especially on the constantly reviewed UI and microtubules determinism has been vastly improved, among with new picker mechanics.
Also tweaks to Evolution view!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f41add3fd449c87358377c27a7258eb745f885e4.png[/img]

[b]PATHWAYS UPDATE[/b]

We're integrating concepts like cellular expansion and stem tissue development in the Pathways, to help players understanding better what to do in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f41add3fd449c87358377c27a7258eb745f885e4.png[/img]

[b]ENDGAME UPDATES 
[/b]
We feel like that lacking a goal makes the game feel more unfinished than it is, so we decided to implement a temporary "end-game" which can give players purpose. 

This structure will reside in extracellular space for now but in the future the end-game itself will be tweaked as more subsystems (circulation, breathing) will be introduced so don't take this as final.

This, massive, hard to build "thing", gives the game an end-goal and a brand-new achievement!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/c75337e81b6f3a8e160fbcaf5315f51def04dc1a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f41add3fd449c87358377c27a7258eb745f885e4.png[/img]

[b]HATCHING AND DEFENDING 
[/b]
As we said in the beginning, a lot of progress has been made towards hemocyte hatching, the primordial immune cell gameplay loop that will introduce exploration and defense from pathogens in the early game.
This infrastructure will be the same mechanics that will be used to produce red blood cells for circulation so it will be nice to have some feedback to help us balance everything.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/00c587cf9342d48498c83004fc8eb428b8daf4bf.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f41add3fd449c87358377c27a7258eb745f885e4.png[/img]

[b]GOALS AND ACHIEVEMENTS
[/b]
All of this will result in new goals and achievements being added to the game, making the experience more complete overall.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f41add3fd449c87358377c27a7258eb745f885e4.png[/img]

[b]MUSIC TRACKS[/b]

In addition, a fresh music track is currently in the works, and we're exploring zone-specific tracks to enhance immersion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/822050dd38e32150389f3fa54d3ff90a7b46adb7.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f41add3fd449c87358377c27a7258eb745f885e4.png[/img]

We're eager to bring you these exciting new developments and will keep you updated as we approach release.

As always, thank you for your continuous feedback and support. Join us on Discord to discuss this update further!

Until next time, keep growing!

notes.title: The road to digestion
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! In recent weeks we’ve been working on many features, we’re going to list some of the major ones below.

Pathfinding system has been completely revamped, which is laying the groundwork for more advanced features like hemocytes breeding (more on that later).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/50b3716a32aa12bfb8a812ea9956bc01cbf3c497.png[/img]
Previously, bubble paths were zig-zagging between chunks, which didn’t feel quite right. We’ve reprogrammed them so that bubble paths are now direct, making them look more organic and move faster.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/e6f1a17d5da17a82263c6a04ee6da41933025eba.gif[/img]
We’ve introduced hemocytes (tiny defensive creatures) as a new type of extracellular defense. You’ll need to breed and grow them. They have their own unique minds and automatically decide where to patrol, defending your extracellular zones from bacterial activity. This brings new extracellular structures: the incubator, the feeder and the niche.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/86eea4c417a7fd552c4d3e1cdedfe2be1a76664b.png[/img]
Almost all the extracellular structures have been redrawn in much more detail to keep the look cohesive with the intracellular zones. Extracellular walls are now thick, as they should be, and structures no longer look pixelated. All buildings now have new unique sound effects, adding to the gurgly experience!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/d02cd824ab973df42d8408376552e68308cc7189.png[/img]
We’ve also started working on a casual mode, which is coincidentally also a mod. This should open the doors to people who think the game is a bit too complicated, making it more accessible to a wider audience.

Diffusers, Dispatchers, and Retrievers have been revamped, and each one now has its primitive version that works without power, offering more options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/a0938d68e92b4688b70a4ba243039738d024fb2c.png[/img]
We’re continually implementing lots of quality-of-life improvements, UI updates, and overall polish to enhance the game. We feel the game is much more mature now; it flows better in many ways!

Expect a new nightly build in the next few days, as we keep working on the public release. 
We'll keep you posted! 

We’ve probably left out a lot of stuff, as usual follow us on Discord where you can see the progress since we post there frequently.

Thanks for reading :)

notes.title: Lifecraft big (literally) updates
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! We've been a bit quiet lately, but time has flown by as we've been hard at work on the digestion update, which is also laying down big foundations of the game core system. 

As we were working on the extracellular systems we noticed that there wasn't enough distinction between the intracellular and extracellular zones, it didn't felt right! That's why we reprogrammed it from the ground so that the extracellular zones now operates on a much larger scale compared to the intracellular gameplay. Integrating these two different mechanics seamlessly required significant rework of the engine but we're finally satisfied with the results! We also have huge extracellular tissue stacks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/11def563f2bf6aaaa590f25d661adfa12487f86f.gif[/img]

We've also worked on the extracellular building and dispatch system. Using tiny bricks you will see the structures grow. It looks really nice and is highly configurable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/6a8d899c641b1bdcb0ef45456cbb204198de485a.gif[/img]

Defending against bacteria in the extracellular space is very important and a mechanic that needed some thought and development. We’ve working on commandable units that you can directly select and move towards bacteria (just like a rts game). This mechanic will be expanded, giving a nice strategic apsect to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/9314c810310319f40708716e6762f6439611f834.png[/img]

We're also continually working on quality of life improvements, UI updates, and overall polish to enhance the game. Microtubules flow algorithm has been rewritten to move all the items simultaneously and feel more coordinated and:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/4299afee9a492c036b96bb75d539848557b1a729.gif[/img]

We made many throughputs of structures precise and predictable so that cytostomes, pickers, microtubules have a precise and shown speed which will help you in optimizing your organism.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/e9926b2a93948e4fe75ba333b2bdfdc506724e42.png[/img]

In the last weeks I’ve been busy creating new music that I think will fit very well the game atmosphere.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/f29ad7ad6802b675c8d0464b799c3c75c8ecfcca.png[/img]

We’ll release the next nightly (available on the nightly branch) in the next days, feel free to test it and give us your feedback on Discord!

(from now on we’ll post more updates here every couple weeks to keep you updated on the game progress, we're kinda lazy with that but we can assure you that on Discord we post a lot of progress day by day!)

notes.title: Lifecraft Primordial Digestion Nightly
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

We're moving toward the first big update of Lifecraft, that will add the first subsystem: digestion! This first part of digestion will include small intestine and it will be a simple way to consume food that will get more complicated over time with future updates.
We spent last 2 months working on a lot of core features of the game that will be used for all the extracellular systems that will come.

This update allows a first primordial digestion through specialized buildings which absorb and dispose of food and a special tank building which is able to digest nutrients and will be used in the future in other subsystems.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/daedae7f4726952386e540d4ab926c569d164f56.png[/img]

We're quite satisfied with the result so far but we had to lay infrastructure for core mechanics like:

[list]
[*] extracellular buildings, which are not directly build but must be build through dispatchers
[*] vessels which can join to structures and can have flows which move elements inside
[*] how to place and retrieve items from vessels
[*] tanks mechanics
[/list]

In addition we spent some time to improve the overall QoL of the game by enhancing controls and UI according to the feedback you all provided.

The update is not ready yet [b][u]but you can freely test the experimental features on the nightly branch[/u][/b] of the game! Mind that these features are still unfinished and require a lot of tweaking.
Don't worry about your save games, the nightly user data is separated from your main game data!

notes.title: Lifecraft Modding
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!
In these days we're working to the new update but meawhile we're investing some time in exploring how modding would integrate with the game. 

The game already supports a basic modding infrastructure but to properly make it work a lot of steps must be taken. Mind that the game is developer on a custom C++ engine so we don't have anything out of the box!

[list]
[*] define a native interface which "exposes" to modders all the feature of the game, this would allow efficient compiled mods as DLLs
[*] choose a scripting language to write mods, to provide a less efficient but easier to use interface
[*] define the bridge between native and scripted interface to bind all the calls
[*] define how to properly manage mods in save games (how to enable/disable them, how to keep track of versions and interactions and so on)
[*] finally implement the functionality on SteamWorks (or even better a custom in game interface) to let you share them in a common way.
[/list]

You can see that this is a [b]LOT[/b] of work, that's why, together with multiplayer, we are slowly doing it in spare time from working on game content.

The overall native API structure has been chosen and it's currently under development, this is a very long process because all the characteristics of the game must be correctly exposed to be altered by mods.

The scripting language chosen is [url=https://www.angelcode.com/angelscript/]AngelScript[/url], which is a really mature scripting language which is able to wrap underlying C++ code in a rather efficient way.

The mapping between native and scripted functions is already started and it automatically generates the documentation:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/cc7e794e31aa7ae4371a159c96bdb4051d82daed.png[/img]

Basic mod loading mechanics is under development, that's not an easy task but something is already working and you can see the final example here:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/3212f2033738293c2344de2a10fc8347d00f011d.png[/img]

This is just a simple example but it's to give you an idea!

[i]TL;DR: modding is long and complicate to implement, some elements are already working and hopefully we'll be able to enable testing your own mods in the nightly branch soon, without much support for sharing them or making them interact but it's a good start anyway.[/i]

Have fun!

notes.title: Microtubules, these strangers
notes.notes:
Today we want to explain some mechanics regarding microtubules.

In our initial (and current) design, microtubules have no direction, only items have it, this means that the same microtubule can be used to move items in any direction as long as an item is moving in any direction over it.
So once an item has momentum it will keep moving, but if you pick and drop it again in the middle of a tubule then it won't start moving again (unless there's a kicker beneath it).

This is quite different from the similar games you're used to and it seemed to have thrown many of our players off course. That's why we're experimenting a new algorithm which simplifies the management through an automatic polarization of microtubules according to how pickers are using them. Let's show this with an example picture which is definitely cleared:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42125058/88dfbaf2b339cbd71d47f4caf3c88bd3290e2033.png[/img]

As you can see, microtubules now have a direction which is dynamically inferred by how they're used by the pickers. As long as there's no ambiguity, then polarization occur and items will move in the specified direction over the tubule.

This system reduces the amount of kickers required and simplifies the management because it's more immediate and intuitive. We feel like it keeps the flexibility but in a simplified way. This new mode is already enabled on the nightly build. So feel free to experiment with it and let us know what you think!

notes.title: Nightly Branch
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

We're working on a lot of additions to the game but in the meanwhile we thought it would have been nice to let you peek and play the content!

That's why we enabled a [b]nightly branch[/b] which can be accessed without any password directly from your Steam clients.

We will use this branch to deploy unfinished features and let you test them, currently we added:

[list]
[*] lysosomes to recycle structures and materials
[*] a new microtubule flow algorithm which automatically decides the flow for your items
[*] a pathways view which explain the main interaction between things in the game, that will be expanded to cover all the game mechanics
[/list]
[i]You can verify the current nightly changelog directly within the game from the changelog button in main menu[/i]

Meanwhile we're working toward first breedable organism (a scout cell!) and  more refined heap management for expansion and possibly internalization of them.

Nightly options and save data won't be shared between the official game and the experimental one (it will be contained in a nightly folder inside the game user data main folder) so this won't affect your game at all, feel free to experiment!

notes.title: macOS and Linux support
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!
You may wonder if we intended to leave macOS and Linux users behind, well the answer is [b]no[/b]!

The game is already compiling and working natively (even on Silicon architecture) on both these platforms so expect prompt support after the Early Access release.

We are deferring these operating systems after launch to first be sure that everything is enough smooth and stable.

Here there are two screenshots to show you what we're talking about:

notes.title: Lifecraft development roadmap
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! Here's a glimpse of what's in the future development pipeline of Lifecraft. Keep in mind that nothing has been set in stone, but we would like to expand every part of the game systems in a very detailed and fun way. 

Depending on the game reception we'll also consider multiplayer and modding, which are two important milestones for the project, we think those will make the game complete in every way. 

Who doesn't want to build cells with their friends? Or maybe plants cells?

See you at release!

notes.title: Lifecraft Open Beta
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!
Today we’re proud to announce the open beta phase of Lifecraft!

The development reached a point in which we feel like the game is mature enough to be played as a free open beta until the launch of the early access release, which will happen most likely at the beginning of 2024.

The game has been polished and refined, we feel like its atmosphere is really becoming what we planned for it and we hope you’ll enjoy playing the game as much as we’re enjoying it.

It’s possible it will be too easy for some of you, or too hard for some others but we’ll try to keep the game options as open as possible to let you enjoy this experience. So please provide us with any feedback you’d like to share!
You can find us on [url=https://discord.gg/TwsNSCHaN8]Discord[/url], together with other fellow players (which we must thank for providing some of the maps used in the open beta teaser).

The development of this game is planned to be a long journey through evolution of a machine as complex as life can be, we hope to engage you to join us.

We plan to release periodic episodes which will add core mechanics to the game, starting with circulation, digestion and respiration but much more will come.
